title: High Agency, Strategy, and Product Work
content:
Demo source notes — original paraphrase, not a verbatim transcript.

High agency in product work can be understood as taking responsibility for outcomes rather than treating constraints as permanent blockers. Useful behaviors include reframing weak problem statements, finding practical paths through dependencies, understanding stakeholder incentives, and continuing to learn when ideal resources are unavailable.

Product managers can improve alignment through concise written proposals and targeted conversations instead of relying only on large meetings. Strong product work also includes deciding what should be removed or simplified when features and workflows create unnecessary complexity.

The practical lesson is to question assumptions, work resourcefully within constraints, protect the core user experience, and optimize for meaningful user value rather than activity.
